Morrow is a private milestone grant system built on Starknet Mainnet with STRK20. It keeps grant terms inspectable, while breaking the permanent public link to the person receiving the funds.

Grant transparency often becomes wallet surveillance. A normal on-chain payout reveals the funder, recipient, amount, timing, and the recipient's future activity as one connected public graph. Morrow separates accountability from identity. The terms stay public. The recipient does not.

Before any transaction, Morrow explains the privacy trade-off. The recommended route is to shield USDC separately, wait for the private note to mature, and only then fund a milestone. Morrow names every public edge and never pretends to calculate a live anonymity score.

Funding is one consequential action. STRK20 withdraws from an existing private balance and invokes MorrowEscrow in the same action batch. The private withdrawal and public milestone lock either succeed together, or the entire operation reverts. No half-funded state is accepted.

Each milestone has two locally generated secrets. The recipient receives the claim secret. The operator keeps a recovery secret for use after the deadline. Morrow shows them once, requires the user to acknowledge saving them, and never places either secret or a recipient address on-chain.

To resolve the grant, the claimant provides the public commitment and matching secret. MorrowEscrow verifies the secret and changes the milestone state once. STRK20 creates the private output, so the public record proves resolution without naming the owner of the resulting note.

This is not only a prototype story. Morrow has three helper-mediated Mainnet proofs. Two transactions funded milestones through the canonical STRK20 pool and MorrowEscrow. A third successfully claimed a milestone, emitted the resolved event, and read back as claimed from the deployed contract.

The Evidence workspace makes that proof easy to inspect. Registered transactions are not accepted from metadata alone. Morrow checks successful Mainnet execution, validates the expected pool or helper event, shows the block, and links directly to the public receipt.

The interface is also designed for a real wallet failure mode. Ready can complete a transaction on-chain while its browser promise remains pending. Morrow now places a time boundary around every request, checks the matching pool or escrow event, and recovers the confirmed hash instead of spinning forever.

The privacy boundary is deliberately precise. Grant terms, amounts, deadlines, helper activity, and timing remain public. Recipient identity, private note ownership, and later private movement stay inside STRK20. Morrow does not call public data private, and does not promise perfect anonymity.
Morrow turns milestone funding into a simple proposition: fund the work, not the surveillance. It is open source, deployed on Starknet Mainnet, and available now as a public Railway application.
